---
title: "Set up AI Superpowers skills on Biowulf"
---

This page shows a beginner-friendly way to set up the shared CCBR Superpowers skills for GitHub Copilot in VS Code on BioWulf.

The goal is simple: install the shared Superpowers resource once, then point each repository to it instead of copying skill files into every project.

## What this is

Superpowers is a shared collection of skills used by GitHub Copilot and other AI coding tools. CCBR keeps the shared version in a central location on Biowulf:

```bash
/data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/superpowers
```

For full implementation details, see the shared installer documentation in:

- [CCBR/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers README](https://github.com/CCBR/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers)
- the repository-level policy in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)

There is also a small installer script for repository setup:

```bash
/data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers/install_superpowers.sh
```

This installer creates the repo-level links and policy files that tell VS Code where the shared skills live.

> The README explains the exact behavior of the installer, and the AGENTS.md section explains the Superpowers usage policy that gets added to each repo.

## Before you start

Make sure you have:

- access to Biowulf
- a Git repository opened in VS Code through Remote SSH
- GitHub Copilot enabled in VS Code
- Agent Skills enabled in VS Code settings (`chat.useAgentSkills`)

If you are a beginner, the easiest way to check is to open a repo in VS Code, then open the Copilot Chat panel and look for the Skills or Configure Skills option.

## Step 1: open the repository you want to configure

From a terminal on Biowulf, go to the repo you want to update:

```bash
cd /path/to/your/repository
```

Then run the installer:

```bash
bash /data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers/install_superpowers.sh
```

You can also run it from any subdirectory inside the repo.

## What the installer does

The installer will:

- create `.github/skills/` if needed
- add symlinks to the shared skill directories in `/data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/superpowers/skills/`
- create or update `AGENTS.md` with the CCBR Superpowers policy section
- leave unrelated project files alone

This means the shared skill definitions stay in one central place, and your repo just points to them.

## Step 2: reload VS Code

After the installer finishes:

1. close the repo folder or reload the VS Code window
2. reopen the repository in the same Remote SSH session
3. make sure GitHub Copilot is active

This reload helps VS Code notice the new `.github/skills` entries.

## Step 3: confirm the skills appeared

Check the folder in your repository:

```bash
ls -l .github/skills
```

You should see entries such as:

```bash
.github/skills/brainstorming -> /data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/superpowers/skills/brainstorming
```

You can also inspect one skill file:

```bash
cat .github/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md
```

If the file opens and shows the skill frontmatter, the setup is working.

## Step 4: test that Copilot sees the skills

In VS Code:

1. open Copilot Chat
2. select the Skills or Configure Skills option
3. look for shared skills such as `brainstorming`
4. ask Copilot to use a skill in a disposable test prompt

For example, try a simple prompt like:

> Use the brainstorming skill to help me plan a small bioinformatics workflow.

If the skill is discovered, Copilot should respond using the shared skill instructions and not just treat it as a normal chat request.

## Common beginner problems

### I do not see the skills in VS Code

Try these steps:

- reload the VS Code window
- confirm the repo root is the one you installed in
- check that `.github/skills` exists and has symlinks
- confirm `chat.useAgentSkills` is enabled

### The installer says there is a conflict

The installer is intentionally careful. If a repo already has a file or directory in the way, it will stop and ask you to resolve it manually instead of overwriting something important.

### The shared path is missing

Ask a CCBR administrator to confirm that the shared install exists and that you have read and execute permissions on:

```bash
/data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/superpowers
```

## Why this is the recommended approach

This shared setup is better than copying skills into each repo because it:

- keeps the skill library in one maintained location
- reduces duplication across projects
- makes updates easier for CCBR admins
- keeps repo-specific policy separate from the shared skill definitions

For the full technical details on how the shared setup is implemented, consult the [CCBR/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers README](https://github.com/CCBR/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers). For the actual repo usage rules, see the CCBR Superpowers policy added to [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).

## Summary

For a CCBR bioinformatician, the normal workflow is:

```bash
cd /path/to/your/repository
bash /data/CCBR_Pipeliner/db/PipeDB/AI/vscode-ghcopilot-superpowers/install_superpowers.sh
```

Then reload VS Code and confirm the skills appear in Copilot Chat.

If the setup works, you are using the shared CCBR Superpowers installation rather than maintaining your own copy.
